- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; smooth forecasts by averaging last 3–5 days’ price + sentiment-weighted adjustment.
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >2% from 14-day moving average, apply mean reversion correction toward prior 14-day average.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model often fails to capture mean reversion; use sentiment as a volatility filter to dampen forecast extremes.
